Can returning Beattie and Haughey make an impact?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021.
  • Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.
  • Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021.

Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.

Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.

Beattie won her last cap a year ago while Haughey will hope to make a senior debut in one of the two games against Greece at Inver Park after she was an unused substitute in friendlies against England and Scotland in her sole call up in 2021.

The inclusion of both players, who have been in good form at their clubs, reveals McArdle is willing to keep the door open for a return to the international squad if players are performing at club level.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies.

Beattie has four goals in her 13 NI caps.

Portsmouth striker Beattie has been in and out of squads since her debut in 2021.

The 24-year-old has four goals in 13 caps, the last of which she won against Iceland in the Nations League play-off a year ago.

A prolific forward during two spells at Glentoran, she has struggled for consistency in moves across to Scotland with the likes of Glasgow City, Hearts and Aberdeen.

She left the Dons in the summer and consulted with McArdle when deciding upon her next move, before joining WSL 2 side Portsmouth.

Beattie has eight goals in all competitions for a Pompey side languishing at the bottom of the table and McArdle is pleased she has settled in well.

"Kerry had spells at Hearts and Aberdeen and for whatever reason it didn't quite work out at both, she had good spells but not a consistent run to express herself," McArdle mentioned.

"The move to Portsmouth, I was delighted she reached out to me for some advice, it's an alignment for her and it's been a great move on and off the pitch. It's allowed her to enjoy herself but also play 90 minutes and be that focal point striker.

"She will have been disappointed not to make the squad for the [World Cup] play-off [against Portugal] with her form but she worked hard and she's back in, I'm delighted for her.".

Beattie faces stiff competition for the starting striker role from the likes of returning captain Simone Magill and Kess Elmore, who impressed in the last camp and scored against Portugal, but she should receive some minutes across the two games and will be keen to grasp her chance to make an impact.

Left-back Haughey was called up to the senior squad as a 16-year-old under Kenny Shiels, but did not feature.

West Brom defender Haughey's last involvement with NI came when she represented the under-19s in 2023.

A Lisburn Rangers player when Kenny Shiels included her in the senior squad as a 16-year-old, Haughey then moved to Nottingham Forest before settling at the Baggies, who play in the National League.

The left-back, 22, has been a regular this season for the club in the third tier and combines playing with her university studies.

Left-back has been a problem position for NI which McArdle has been trying to address as demonstrated by him bringing in Lucy-Jayne Grant in the last camp and Haughey for this window to allow Rebecca Holloway to play as a central defender.

Haughey will be competing with Grant to fill that full-back role on the left side and McArdle believes she is more than capable of doing so having tried to bring her back into the squad earlier in his reign.

"Ella's been at West Brom for a few years now. She has real potential, strong, athletic potential. We tried to call her up sooner but there were some challenges," he explained.

"She's probably been one of their top performers and one of the top performers in the league. Delighted she's earned this opportunity and hopefully she can make her debut and achieve her first cap.".

McArdle has made a concerted to continue to widen the player pool available to him as he aims to build depth ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, but if Beattie and Haughey catch the eye it will show that giving chances to those previously involved under different managers could be another possibility.

Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season.

The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies.

Sources indicate that we compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL challenges. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes.

Even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the massive question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove.

The arrival of winter is perhaps leading to some frustration, particularly in front of goal. Arsenal remain unbeaten but they were punished for not taking their opportunities as they dropped points at home to Borussia Dortmund, a result which means their place in the top-eight is not assured yet ahead of tough games against Real Madrid and Real Betis.

Real Madrid have come into a remarkable run of form, with a thumping win over PSV making it 10 wins in a row in all competitions under Jose Mourinho. It’s funny, in the Champions League, Real Madrid have trailed several games yet have maximum points. Now, the 15-time Champions League winners are not just managing to find a way, but they are blowing teams off the park.

It has been revealed that before Andoni Iraola’s first season, it felt like so much depended on the potential of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz coming good in the Liverpool attack. Well, the signs of the past few weeks have been hugely promising as Isak and Wirtz continued to build their partnership in the 3-0 win at Club Brugge, with the Reds bouncing back from their shock defeat at Fenerbahce last time out.

According to recent reports, the major concern for the German champions is the fitness of their Ballon d’Or holder Harry Kane, who will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury. Bayern have plenty of games to play until then and the question is whether they can get through to the top eight without Kane to avoid an additional play-off round. A stunning 2-1 defeat at Lille, which featured some calamitous defending and a truly remarkable Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal (honestly, go and check it out...), saw Bayern drop to 15th in the table.

Three defeats from four in the Premier League have well and truly taken shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. After another sloppy performance against Napoli and the returning Kevin De Bruyne means it is now 10 games in a row without a clean sheet. City now face a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona and likely require a result to avoid dropping out of the top eight.

Up at the top of the table with the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Barcelona, the Champions League debutants are certainly making a name for themselves. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side didn’t quite hit the same heights against AEK Athens after their nine-goal dismantling of poor Lens, but look what comes next. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase, after a tricky trip to Real Betis, are going to be fascinating.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, Inter have responded with three consecutive wins. There was more good news in the 2-0 win over Stuttgart as Lautaro Martinez marked his return from injury after a month on the sidelines with a goal.

Sure, they absolutely bottled it against Real Madrid and Manchester United, throwing away leads on both occasions. Sure, they’ve got five points from five games in the Champions League and sit outside the top 24 in the league table. But a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain continued Roma’s impressive season under Gian Piero Gasperini; they remain unbeaten in Serie A and now have a more favourable run of games in the Champions League. On performances alone, they’ve earned a place in our top 10.

It has been revealed that ⬇️ 🔴 15. Manchester United (-1).

Disney beats fourth-quarter estimates, targets $3 billion in savings through cost-cutting efforts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1161 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and confirmed it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.
  • Recent findings suggest that those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs announced in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and confirmed it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.

Recent findings suggest that those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs announced in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC. The most recent round, which seeks to reduce costs by up to 20%, was reported earlier this month.

Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston said, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs.".

Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro told investors on the firm's earnings call that the job cuts are "not easy.".

"They affect people who care deeply about Disney and have contributed so much to this company," he said. "At the same time, these steps are crucial if we want to be a company that moves faster, adapts to a rapidly changing environment, and keeps investing in the content and technology that will drive our growth.".

The cuts will help Disney fund its $26 billion in projected content spend for fiscal 2027, a 9% increase from fiscal 2026.

The entertainment giant is also forecasting double-digit growth in earnings per share in the next fiscal year, as well as segment operating income growth of around 8%.

Disney noted that the majority of that growth will be concentrated in the first half of the year due to the theatrical debut of "Avengers: Doomsday" and a boost from the Super Bowl, which will air on Disney's ESPN and ABC networks.

It has been revealed that "The growth is really going to come in the first half of this year," Johnston said. "That's the opposite of what we saw in '26, where the growth was backloaded.".

In a recent development, the company will also increase its annual dividend to $2 a share, a 33% increase from the previously declared dividend. It will be payable in two installments of $1 per share, one in January and one in July.

Here's how Disney performed in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Oct. 3, compared with what Wall Street expected, according to LSEG:.

Disney reported net income for the fiscal fourth quarter of $2.61 billion, or $1.51 per share, compared with $1.31 billion, or 73 cents per share, during the same period the year prior.

Adjusting for one-time items, including severance and other restructuring charges as well as the value of intangible assets, Disney reported earnings per share of $1.77.

The company's revenue for the quarter was 16% higher year over year, and results were once again lifted by its parks and streaming divisions.

Disney's experiences segment, which includes its theme parks and cruises, reported nearly $10.11 billion in revenue, up 15% year over year. Operating income for the unit increased 20% to $2.25 billion.

The division is already a top performer for the company, but it benefited in the fiscal fourth quarter because of an extra calendar week compared with the previous fiscal year.

While international attendance continues to lag at Disney's domestic parks, it is being offset by domestic attendance, especially at the Walt Disney World resort in Orlando, Florida, Johnston stated.

Growth at Disneyland Paris was driven by recent investments including an expansion area called World of Frozen. Attendance at the Hong Kong and Shanghai parks remained soft because of broad economic challenges in those regions, according to Disney.

Still, D'Amaro mentioned he believes the growth in parks will be sustainable through next year, especially with fresh additions, including the "Monsters, Inc."-themed land "Monstropolis" opening at Walt Disney World in 2027.

Industry observers note that "Q1 forward resort bookings at Walt Disney World are pacing up compared to the prior year," he remarked. "And newly introduced capacity and new experiences will start coming online in 2027. We keep investing to make the experience fresh, and what we see is that drives repeat visits.".

The manufacturer expects operating income for the experiences segment to grow in the high-single digits in fiscal 2027. Growth is expected to be front-loaded as the company laps the launch of the Disney Adventure cruise ship, which set sail in March.

Over at its entertainment division, Disney saw revenue increase 17% to $11.89 billion. Operating income nearly doubled to $1.33 billion.

Revenue from streaming, specifically, rose 19% to $6.1 billion, Disney mentioned.

In a recent development, the segment benefited from the extra week on the fiscal calendar as well as from growth in subscription and affiliate fees. Additionally, the company saw higher theatrical distribution revenue from titles like "Toy Story 5.".

Disney stated Tuesday it expects operating income for the entertainment division to grow in the high-single digits in the coming fiscal year.

The firm's sports division saw revenue increase 16% in the fiscal fourth quarter, reaching $4.61 billion. Operating income for the segment surged more than 50% to $1.39 billion.

Subscription and affiliate fees fueled this growth alongside an increase in advertising revenue.

The firm expects its sports division's operating income to grow by double digits in fiscal 2027. It noted that the fiscal first quarter of the year will see some declines because of the timing of College Football Playoff games and the New Year's window. However, the fiscal second quarter will benefit from the college championship as well as the broadcast of Super Bowl 61.

Disney's outlook for overall and segment results for fiscal 2027 excludes the impact of a 53rd week in fiscal 2026.

D'Amaro has made advancing technology a pillar of the tech giant's growth strategy. In September, Disney hired Karandeep Anand in the newly created position of chief technology officer.

Sources indicate that "Technology is central to how we connect fans to more of Disney and drive returns on our investment," D'Amaro said on the earnings call. "[Anand has] been energized by how much opportunity he sees to move faster and go further in product and technology. Done right, that means serving our fans even better, working more efficiently and being more innovative across every one of our businesses.".

Disney announced a partnership with Adobe earlier this month to develop generative artificial intelligence models.

D'Amaro told investors that the team is exploring ways to use AI to make booking trips to Disney parks easier.

"There's actually a vacation planning tool that's in beta right now at Walt Disney World. We built that with our partners at Google, and I've had a chance to experiment with it myself," he said. "It'll be incredibly helpful for our guests who are booking trips. With these AI features, it can feel like you've got someone sitting right by your side, like a personal concierge, that plans and responds to the way that you want to actually book your trip to Walt Disney World.".

According to recent reports, the entertainment organization has also expanded its short-form content, adding a vertical video channel within the Disney+ mobile app. The company had previously revealed a partnership with TikTok to bring creator content to the streaming app.

#140861. Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year.
  • According to recent reports, A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland.
  • In a recent development, bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

Words by Saugat Bolakhe and photos by CJ Karki.

According to recent reports, A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland. Beneath a canopy of pines, Himalayan chestnuts and Nepalese alders, the group listens as wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal guides them through a questionnaire designed to document the signs of poaching.

In a recent development, bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity. But instead of focusing on animals, as many conservation projects do, the group’s objective is to protect flora, specifically orchids. These flowering plants are harvested and sold across Nepal’s borders.

The flowers are prized for their ornamental value, but they are also used in traditional medicines, including Chinese, Tibetan and Ayurveda healing products.

Sources indicate that multiple parts of the plant, including the stem and fruit, can also be used as ingredients. “It’s as if these plants have some magical properties about them,” Bashyal indicates.

Nepal has more than 500 orchid species, many of which are heavily harvested. Between 2008 and 2016, the country legally exported more than 47,000 kilograms of wild-collected orchids. However, discrepancies exist between Nepal’s export data and those of its trading partners, arising from challenges such as mismatched and unreported trade amounts and species being sold under different names.

According to recent reports, the trade in animal and plant species is regulated mostly under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) agreement, which is designed to protect wildlife from exploitation. Although Nepal joined the convention more than 50 years ago, it did not introduce legislation to implement CITES until 2017.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

It has been revealed that all but two species of orchid in Nepal are now listed in CITES Appendix II, which includes species that are not currently threatened with extinction but could be if their trade is not regulated. The government must create a management initiative and a formal assessment to confirm that harvesting a species for trade won’t harm the survival of the wild population. “We haven’t prepared such a management plan for any orchid species yet. So, their trade is still considered illegal here,” Bashyal adds. Violation of the CITES Act can lead to a fine of up to 100,000 Nepalese rupees (US$660), one year in prison, or both.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Recent findings suggest that bashyal first became involved in orchid research by chance. In 2018, while working on a conifer tree conservation project for non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal in Kathmandu, she visited several regional sites across the country and was often approached by people asking about the demand for orchids in the city. When her team investigated further, it realized that many people living in the villages were harvesting or actively trading the plants.

This illegal trading was often overlooked by authorities, according to Bashyal. Before suggesting a way to stop it, the team had to understand the market — specifically which species were being taken, their conservation status and how the supply chain operated. To do this, it visited orchid trading hubs across Nepal and spoke to harvesters, traders and enforcement officials.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

“The local people provide information on where orchids are harvested, moved, gathered and how much they sold orchids for,” she indicates. During these visits, the team shared its research and spoke about the importance of conservation, which was well received, she says. “After all, an unsustainable harvesting of the orchids severely threatens local livelihood and income,” she adds.

Sources indicate that bashyal’s team at Greenhood Nepal learnt that several orchid species, including Satyrium nepalense and Pleione praecox, are harvested in large quantities for their medicinal value. Overharvesting an orchid species that is in decline can easily lead to its extinction in the wild, which makes understanding a species’ population and distribution crucial for creating sustainable harvesting practices.

After the field trips, Bashyal’s team created a series of policy briefs, drafted conservation frameworks and started the anti-poaching taskforce in collaboration with the region’s governmental forest management office to document illegal activity and conduct patrols.

Industry observers note that the team is also developing comprehensive identification manuals and guidelines for regulators. Many existing manuals focus on identifying whole plants and flowers, but traded items can include the orchid’s thickened stem and fleshy underground storage organs, called tubers. Some orchids are boiled, or dried for several hours or days before being traded.

Sources indicate that in some parts of Nepal, communities can earn a good income from harvesting and selling orchids alongside other medicinal plants. For many, medicinal plants are their sole source of income. “Simply telling the locals ‘you are not supposed to do this’ will not stop them from harvesting,” Bashyal notes. For this reason, imposing a blanket ban on trade might not be effective.

Bashyal emphasizes that tracking the wildlife trade is complex and often requires navigating delicate legal territory. Researchers must also have patience when interviewing informants. “Thus, it also comes down to following research ethics, respect and treating local knowledge as a valuable resource to build trust,” Bashyal says. “Only after that, can we have data and develop any intervention.”.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

Kelly Somers has recalled a deeply personal moment with Sir Gareth Southgate after England’s victory over Germany at Euro 2020 – and a thoughtful gesture the former Three Lions manager made when she was pregnant.

Sir Gareth's England beat Germany 2-0 at Wembley in June 2021, 25 years after his decisive penalty miss against the same opponents in the Euro 96 semi-finals, and the result prompted an emotional reflection on the team-mates he felt he had let down all those years ago.

As the BBC’s England reporter, Somers was there to capture that reaction, and claims it remains one of the standout conversations of her time following the national side.

Asked for her favourite interviews over her years covering England, Somers told FourFourTwo: “[Southgate] noted he’d looked up to the major screen midway through the game and seen David Seaman sitting there.

“He said 'I know I can never undo any of the heartache I caused them, but hopefully this has gone a long way'. Hearing him say that was really special.”.

Somers was also touched by an off-camera gesture delivered by Southgate during her pregnancy in 2023.

She said: “When I was pregnant in 2023, Gareth gave me a little England kit for my daughter in a gift bag.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“In true Gareth Southgate fashion, he remarked 'I didn’t actually know about your pregnancy, my team arranged this, but this is on behalf of the FA'.

"He didn’t want to take the credit for it, which I thought was lovely.”.

Somers also picked out interviewing Ollie Watkins dramatic winner against the Netherlands in the Euro 2024 semi-final as a highlight.

She mentioned: "It felt like I was talking to a boy from the park, I was speaking to someone at pretty much the pinnacle of their life.

Industry observers note that “There was another where I had to wait for Jude Bellingham after a drugs test, and he came out in just his top and pants. I thought ‘This is all very weird!’ But he’s always very good in interviews.".

It has been revealed that somers added: "To be the in-camp reporter is incredible, because pretty much every day you get 15 minutes with a different player, so I’ve got to know them. I love interviewing and the challenge of bringing out the human side of players.

Sources indicate that "At the Euros in 2021, I did one with Jack Grealish where he spoke about his sister – he’s incredibly close to his family. When the interview ended, he mentioned “I was getting emotional, I didn’t expect that.”.

Published: 16:06 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:16 EST, 26 November 2026.

European football has endured another night of chaos with fan trouble at Marseille, Besiktas, and Sunderland.

Fans of Marseille and Levski Sofia clashed violently at their Europa League match, with home hooligans descending on the away end with bats and metal pipes after being provoked by a Nazi salute.

Turkish side Besiktas' clash with Israeli team Hapoel Be'er Sheva was brought to a temporary halt after fans of the former unfurled a pro-Palestinian flag, leading to a clash with police.

And Sunderland's home end was infiltrated by supporters of Jagiellonia Bialystok, who had been banned for the fixture by UEFA - with some of the visitors starting brawls.

The three Europa League disturbances cast another dark shadow over football.

Marseille saw the worst events as an estimated 200-300 home hooligans entered the away end with bats, pipes, and flares.

Marseille's supporters descended on the Levski Sofia end with bats and flares.

It is believed that the Marseille ultras were provoked by a Nazi salute by a Levski Sofia fan.

One supporter at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match nursed a bleeding head injury.

Besiktas fans unfurled a Palestine flag at their fixture against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

They had reportedly been provoked by some of Levski's ultras, who have a long association with neo-Nazism, and Marseille's supporters responded with an antifascist chant.

Some people kicked and punched each other - another even used a fire extinguisher, according to L'Equipe.

Bulgarian news agency Bgnes reported that the French hooligans also hurled bottles, flares and firecrackers.

Women and members of Levski's entourage were among the crowd, and several injured supporters had to be escorted out of the stadium, according to reports.

'Olympique de Marseille condemns the incidents that occurred on the sidelines of the match against Levski Sofia,' the hosts mentioned in a statement.

'The swift intervention of the club's security teams restored calm, without affecting the match itself.

'The club is currently working to establish the precise circumstances of these incidents, in conjunction with the relevant authorities.'.

Meanwhile, trouble spiked in the 25th minute of Besiktas' 2-1 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

One fan was seen being taken away on a stretcher at the Besiktas game, which was played in Batumi, Georgia.

Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the advertising hoarding, covering the UEFA lettering.

Police had to remove some Jagiellonia Bialystok fans who had infiltrated the home end at Sunderland.

According to recent reports, the match had been moved to Batumi, Georgia due to security worries surrounding ties between Turkish and Israeli clubs. There was even tension on the pitch, as Besiktas refused to shake hands with their opponents.

Sources indicate that after a pro-Palestine banner was revealed by Besiktas' fans, the Georgian police appeared to react with tear gas or pepper spray and batons. One fan was seen being carried away on a stretcher.

The game had to be briefly suspended, with both sets of teams and the officials going to the dressing rooms.

After the match, Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the UEFA lettering on the pitchside advertising hoardings.

Besiktas condemned the local police, saying they had used 'disproportionate force'.

The club also wrote: 'Upon learning that security forces were obstructing our fans' entry into the stadium, we immediately contacted the UEFA delegate, who arranged for the stadium's evacuation gates to be opened, allowing our fans to enter the stadium rapidly and safely.

'We announce that steps have been taken with our Consulate General in Batumi and UEFA regarding the disproportionate force used by security forces against our fans, and state that we will closely monitor the situation until each of our fans returns safely to our country.'.

Turkey and Israel have long been simmering with tension amid the conflict and numerous Turkish clubs such as Galatasaray, Fenerbahce, and Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor came out in support of Besiktas later - despite usually being bitter rivals.

A UEFA Disciplinary ruling meant Polish club Jagiellonia Białystok weren't meant to have any away supporters at The Stadium of Light for tonight's game at Sunderland, yet plenty of them have turned up in the home end… 🫣😭pic.twitter.com/lRBvHOp16T.

Jagiellonia Bialystok's supporters had been banned - but some bought tickets in the home end.

Meanwhile, at the Stadium of Light, events were of a lower scale, but some away fans were seen brawling with the home faithful and police waded in to eject them.

Jagiellonia Bialystok's fans had been banned from attending the game by UEFA following disturbances between them and Levski Sofia fans earlier this month.

But around 20 of them managed to secure tickets, Sunderland believe, and squeeze into the stadium.

The club had already caught some out in advance, writing: 'The club is actively monitoring ticket purchases and has identified and cancelled tickets purchased by, or on behalf of, individuals identified as Jagiellonia supporters.

'All affected tickets will be refunded to the original purchasers.

'This restriction applies across all areas of the stadium, including home sections, and regardless of how tickets have been purchased or transferred.

'Any attempt to circumvent the restriction, including using tickets purchased through third parties or belonging to other supporters, will result in refusal of entry.

'Jagiellonia supporters without a valid entitlement to attend the fixture are strongly advised not to travel to Sunderland.

'No Jagiellonia supporters without valid permission to attend will be permitted entry into the Stadium of Light, and we strongly advise they stay away from the immediate surrounding vicinity.

'The club will continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to ensure UEFA's ruling is fully enforced and that the fixture takes place as a home supporter-only event.'.

Mauricio Pochettino was proud of Manchester United’s performance and his players’ early progress in the action-packed 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The former Argentina international began his reign with a chastening 4-0 loss at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, when Leny Yoro’s early – and subsequently overturned – red card was the catalyst for Anfield agony.

More frustration followed on Wednesday, when Senne Lammens gifted Sporting a penalty converted by Luis Suarez shortly after denying him from the spot before Bruno Fernandes’ double with the help of a bobble put United in front.

But Suarez would level in the second half after nudging Lammens when attempting to gather a high ball and Pochettino’s hopes of a first win ended when home goalkeeper Kaique Pereira’s own goal was ruled out.

Szymon Marciniak adjudged Patrick Dorgu to have fouled him having been sent to the monitor on a night when the referee’s early whistle meant a disallowed first half Amad Diallo goal could not be overturned.

Youri Tielemans was incorrectly booked for his role in that incident and picked up a second booking at the end of an eventful night that saw Pochettino focus on the positives in Portugal.

According to recent reports, “I am so proud of our players, my players,” Pochettino told TNT Sports. “It was a really tough game.

Sources indicate that “I like the team during 90 minutes, the personality, the character. And it’s true that it’s difficult to find some game that (you will) be more punished.

“We were punished a lot in different actions that were key, but I think everyone that watched the game saw all the action.

According to recent reports, “Only what I can say is I feel proud about the players. I think we today highlighted the way that we want to play. It’s only one week working together. I feel so proud. I told them after the game.”.

Referee Marciniak’s poor performance will dominate the fallout to the draw at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, as will goalkeeper Lammens’ latest shaky display in a season replete with individual errors by United players.

Recent findings suggest that “Always we need to do double effort,” Pochettino said. “We need to concentrate more and focus more and try to (do) recovery better, do all the effort.

“I think in this type of situation we start to fix also with results, but with (a) performance like today that is for me is the best medicine to prepare the next game.”.

Pochettino’s frantic start to life in charge continues on Saturday afternoon at Old Trafford, where he will take charge of United for the first time against Brentford.

The embattled Red Devils have just one win to show from their opening 11 Premier League matches and languish 19th in the standings.

Sources indicate that “I think we need to encourage and we need to really believe in our play,” Pochettino added. “We need to believe more and more and more.

“I think we need to give the capacity and the tools to perform and of course improving things.

“But that is the way that we need to show our aggression, like in the second half. We recover a lot of ball in the opposite half.

“We were aggressive, and I think I think that is the way that we want to play.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be nice to people on your way up, because you'll meet them on your way down – whether you're Wayne Rooney at Everton, Theo Walcott at Southampton or just expecting to queue with the same crowd on a return flight from Madrid.

It's 8am on a Saturday though, and while plenty of the punters have dropped off luggage, FourFourTwo are doing no such thing, travelling light for a hit-and-run mission to Spain: yep, we're coming back here tomorrow.

Welcome to the era of 'Trip Snacking': the only sights we're taking in are Jose Mourinho's thousand-yard stare, Jude Bellingham's outstretched arms and the wonder of learning that Iago Aspas, pushing 40, is still getting wheeled out on the biggest stages of all. We're here for a prime cut of La Liga, and this time, you can keep your museums, palaces and fancy sky bars.

It has been revealed that fourFourTwo have always loved a quick turnaround – the relentless nature of European away days practically dictates it – but the concept has officially gone mainstream. According to Hotels.com’s Unpack ’27 travel trends report, Trip Snacking is the defining travel trend of 2027. It's the rise of the one-night stay – the loan spell of the tourism world – precision-engineered to fit seamlessly around packed schedules and tighter budgets, with fans increasingly turning match-day into getaway-day. Count us in.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers speak for themselves. Searches for one-night stays are up nearly 10 per cent year-on-year globally, and up 15 per cent among British travellers. Some 73 per cent of travellers booked a one-night stay in the past 12 months, and 79 per cent say they are planning to book one in the coming year, climbing to 83 per cent among Millennials and Gen Z.

While 42 per cent cite celebrating life milestones and 23 per cent simply need a quick reset between traditional holidays, a massive 49 per cent of Brits are doing it to attend concerts, shows and sporting events.

That's why we're here. Madrid is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the trend: weekend lodging searches to the Spanish capital during the football season are up 20 per cent year-on-year, while full-season searches have risen 25 per cent. It's a pattern repeating across Europe's major footballing hubs – demand has surged in Liverpool (up 100 per cent), Manchester (up 95 per cent), London (up 40 per cent) and Munich (up 10 per cent). Unsurprisingly, marquee European nights drive the biggest spikes, with Madrid searches jumping 70 per cent around a clash with Bayern Munich, and Manchester rising 25 per cent when Los Blancos came to town.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

As an Official Partner of Real Madrid, Hotels.com arranged our stay at the five-star Barcelo Imagine – one of their top-rated picks for a Madrid football break, starting at £125 per night – purely for Real hosting Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu. On a 24-hour getaway, staying close to the action is half the battle.

According to recent reports, A quick drop of the bags and we're out into the crisp Madrid afternoon. It's warm for November, ideal for a stroll up towards the Bernabeu, semi-newly renovated – looking a little like a giant airfryer – and packed with fans and tourists alike. Thanks to our hosts, FourFourTwo took in the action from the Hotels.com VIP box, situated just behind the goal. The PA system is booming – a little like we imagine Mourinho will be when Real return to the dressing room for the half-time break trailing by a goal. But we came here to have superstars, and the Special One appears obliging to treat us to a fair few from his bench.

A beautiful five-star hotel just a five-minute Uber from the Bernabeu, the Barcelo Imagine is a superb choice to stay at for Trip snacking. The seasonal outdoor pool is a great spot to take a dip, and guests can grab a bite to eat at Eat & Roll, which serves local and international cuisine and is open for breakfast. Other highlights at this luxurious hotel include 2 bars/lounges, a poolside bar and a fitness centre.

Sources indicate that vinicius Jr has struggled early on this season but is now back to his sparkling best, grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck and toying with his full-back like a cat with string. Pretty soon after his introduction, the stadium is dancing to a samba rhythm, led by the Brazilian orchestrating with ease – and after Bellingham's punchy equaliser, Los Blancos really step up a gear. It's a lesser-known name, Carlos Espi, who grabs the winner from close range, letting out a primal roar in front of the Grada Fans, reflecting 80,000 relieved Madridistas, all exhaling at once.

In the end, Celta simply couldn't keep up, as we discuss after the game. This is where the true joy of the Madrid Trip Snack begins: a late dinner means midnight tapas, swapping stories, and dissecting the match over plates of jamon iberico and patatas bravas. Some 32 per cent of travellers say they have taken a one-night trip specifically for a sporting event – rising to 33 per cent among women – and turning a 90-minute match into a 24-hour cultural immersion feels like the ultimate life hack.

Recent findings suggest that as Melanie Fish, Hotels.com spokesperson and travel expert, puts it: "Football fans aren't waiting for a week-long holiday anymore. They're turning matches into memorable 24-hour getaways, whether that's a weekend in Madrid or a European away game." For Trip Snackers, finding a good deal is key, and perks like free cancellation and earning £100 in Hotels.comCash after 10 nights make squeezing in a spontaneous trip much easier to justify.

Sources indicate that sunday morning allows for no such gentle reset – we're going back to the Bernabeu for a tour of the stadium, believe it or not – before heading off to the airport, roughly 24 hours after we arrived. We feel a little like an away team, jetting into the city just for the game, enjoying a warm down and getting back for Match of the Day 2 – but we crammed in enough football, croquettes and merch from the Real club shop that it feels like we were away longer than just a day.

An impressive 71 per cent of travellers agree that a Trip Snack holds them over until their next longer trip, and it is easy to see why. We do not always have the time, the annual leave, or the funds for a sprawling European tour. We cannot all travel the continent watching our team – especially when it's Real Madrid, who have been to Rome and Athens already this autumn, with London on tfhotelshe horizon.

In a recent development, sometimes, you just need a quick fix. Sometimes it takes heading to the nation of tapas to realise you just need a bite over a buffet.

He has written cover features for the mag on Mikel Arteta and Martin Odegaard, and is assisted by his cat, Rosie, who has interned for the brand since lockdown.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home Depot on Tuesday revealed its chief financial officer, Richard McPhail, will become CEO of the tech giant, succeeding Ted Decker, effective next week.

Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot stated Ann-Marie Campbell, at the moment senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to succeed McPhail.

It has been revealed that decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said.

According to recent reports, "I'm glad to be back and grateful for the support I received," Decker told analysts on Tuesday. "The board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession initiative.".

McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles.

"We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick.

According to recent reports, he stated the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using artificial intelligence tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market.

Sources indicate that home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the firm has previously noted it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects.

Shares of Home Depot sank more than 3% following the announcement and the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results.

The CEO change came as the home improvement retailer posted quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations. The company remarked comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount.

Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

The company reported net income of $3.71 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.60 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86.

Revenue rose 4.9% compared with the year-ago period.

"We also are confident that we are taking material share from the market and from competition," McPhail said on the call with analysts.

In the third quarter, the organization stated online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric.

The manufacturer mentioned it saw positive comparable sales numbers in 13 out of 16 of its merchandising departments, including notable strength in the power department, which posted double-digit percentage growth.

Industry observers note that for the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase.

Home Depot added it expects adjusted earnings per share to rise 2% this year, compared with prior guidance of flat to a 4% increase.

This blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of headlines from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.

The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.

You can read details on what has been happening at the top football club in this DW article: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has stated.

The family stated in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later stated in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

Recent findings suggest that according to his family, Flick once said: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

"Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It said the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an crucial bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG said it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an vital shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," said Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also stated that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It noted species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig says that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

Industry observers note that "Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she said, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She said that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), noted she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She said that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are presently being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

The powerful IG Metall union stated on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding firm Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union said that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It says that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

The DW newsroom says "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.

Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.

In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.

And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has stated it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.

Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.

Recent findings suggest that we're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!

A fresh goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

Sources indicate that after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

However, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke said he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

Fourth-place RB Leipzig had five different players score in a 5-1 victory over Union Berlin, bringing them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen scored four unanswered goals against Paderborn to stay in fifth place.

Germany is seeking to redress years of underinvestment by pouring billions into the modernization of public infrastructure and digital networks, and the transition to renewable energy sources.

But will the proposal bring real change amid the labor shortages, burdensome bureaucracy and low productivity right now besetting Europe's largest economy?

DW takes a look at what is one of Germany's biggest public investment drives in decades in this video:.

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

Recent findings suggest that operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

Sources indicate that bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

"We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen mentioned. "This shows that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

Industry observers note that moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer noted.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

Bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

Two and a half weeks after his sudden death, Free Voters leader Hubert Aiwanger, who was Bavarian Minister of Economic Affairs and Deputy Minister-President, was laid to rest in his hometown of Inkofen in Lower Bavaria.

A memorial service was held at the Parish Church of the Presentation of the Lord and broadcast on a screen outside. According to the organizers, around 2,000 people attended the solemn service.

Aiwanger's funeral was open to the public. His longtime partner, Tanja Schweiger, the Regensburg district administrator (Free Voters), stated that Aiwanger had been "a man of the people.".

Sources indicate that for that reason, she said, everyone "who liked and appreciated him" was warmly welcome. The politician had already been honored with a state funeral in Munich a week earlier.

Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel on November 4 after canceling an appointment for health reasons. The 55-year-old died of natural causes.

Industry observers note that “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” mentioned Iraola.

Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the new format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February.

Recent findings suggest that “I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” remarked Iraola.

On Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily.

It has been revealed that “The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations.

In a recent development, “In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit.

“Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.”.

Isak stated he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”.

Sources indicate that he added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.”.

Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish.

“Both are now in a good place,” he stated. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse.

In a recent development, “The crucial part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”.

Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
  • In a recent development, the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

In a recent development, the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 presently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" concerns.

Users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of Upcoming York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer says physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

Industry observers note that the Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting upcoming type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

Sources indicate that "We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

In a recent development, the social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's new military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Recent findings suggest that haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he remarked.

Agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

"It is an omission of the parties," he stated. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

Industry observers note that the center-left and center-right major-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

It has been revealed that party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) showed that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

According to recent reports, in the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

The political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

Joshua Kimmich has criticised Bayern Munich over their handling of teammate Jamal Musiala, describing the club’s public conduct towards the midfielder — who suffers from a neurological condition that causes seizures — as "not Bayern-like".

The comments follow public criticism from senior figures at Bayern regarding Musiala’s performances and contract. The player experienced two seizures on the pitch during pre-season fixtures, prompting opposition from the international players' union, FIFPRO.

A key squad member has now spoken out, warning that the club risks damaging its traditional family values.

"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. "It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either.".

Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's ongoing struggles were more closely linked to physical injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at last year's Club World Cup, rather than his medical condition.

Recent findings suggest that "It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.

Bayern met with Musiala's representatives on Tuesday to clarify the timeline of events, rejecting speculation that the midfielder concealed his health condition prior to signing his recent contract extension.

Both the club and Musiala's representatives accept that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after extending his contract.

"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern stated.

Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the pitch during two pre-season matches, alarming fans and fellow professionals.

It has been revealed that bayern coach Vincent Kompany stated at the time that the episodes were triggered by a change in Musiala's medication. He was rested for the start of the campaign and has since missed games due to a muscle injury.

Recent findings suggest that musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Wednesday's defeat at Lille, capping a difficult week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga and fallen to 15th in the Champions League standings.

Manchester City are considering the future of manager Enzo Maresca, just 19 games into the Italian's stint.

After Pep Guardiola led the Citizens to 20 trophies in a decade-long tenure, Manchester City turned to Maresca to take charge of the club, with the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss having worked at the Etihad as both the under-23s manager and as one of Guardiola's assistants in the 2022/23 Treble-winning campaign.

But with uncertainty shrouding the club – following an independent commission finding City guilty of over 100 breaches of serious financial rules across a nine-year period – things may be about to become even more unstable, should the six-time Premier League champions pull the trigger on their manager already.

Maresca started fantastically after taking over from his former mentor, winning his first seven Premier League games – including a defiant 3-0 thumping of Liverpool at Anfield following the news that City had been found guilty and were facing Premier League sanctions.

But the Eastlands outfit went on to lose the following three games in the league, drew against Fulham at the weekend, and had to rely on a late Rayan Cherki equaliser against Napoli last night in order to scrape a point in the Champions League.

Fichajes in Spain are reporting that Maresca “will be fighting for his job” if he doesn't beat Arsenal this weekend, with the Gunners having already outclassed his side 3-0 in the Community Shield earlier this season.

A defeat at the Emirates Stadium would widen the gap between the pair to a seemingly unassailable nine points, with Liverpool and surprise package Brighton & Hove Albion shaping up to be the champions' biggest threats in completing back-to-back league championships for the first time in almost a century.

While City started the season emphatically, fans have questioned several tactical decisions – and after netting seven in his first seven fixtures, talismanic centre-forward Erling Haaland has cut a frustrated figure while leading the line.

Record signing Enzo Fernandez has blown hot and cold this season and kept the mercurial Cherki out of the side at times, Marc Guehi has started the season slowly with shaky performances from centre-back, and Phil Foden has been in disappointing form in the league, though he netted a hat-trick against AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Several of Guardiola's generals have been linked with exits, with Haaland's future in doubt, while Barcelona have interest in Josko Gvardiol to fill a problem position at left-back.

Despite the autumnal wobble, however, FourFourTwo understands that there are no looks at present to part with Maresca.

The Italian was handed a three-year deal over the summer to succeed Guardiola, with BBC Sport reporting that City paid around £17 million to Maresca's former club Chelsea as a compensation fee after he left the Blues in January 2026, following run of just one win in seven league games.

City's clash with Arsenal is set for 4.30pm this Sunday as Premier League action resumes.

Now the 22 year-old American is the joint-leading scorer in the Scottish Premiership, with eight goals from 11 starts.

His tremendous form has helped Falkirk surge up the table, with six successive victories taking them from 11th to third place.

"I was looking for more minutes as a young player and Falkirk kind of came out of nowhere," he explained. "They called my agent and a week later I was in Scotland.

"Stepping out of my comfort zone has taught me a lot about myself, having to adapt and grow up.".
